evidence: The wafers were then transferred to the chamber of an ALD system (Picosun SUNALE TM R-150B, Finland), and a 6 nm-thick Al2O3 layer (60 cycles) was deposited at 300 /C14 C using trimethylaluminum (TMA) and H 2O as the precursors and N 2 (99.999%) as the carrier/purge gas. 27 Subsequently, ALD was performed to perform ex situ or in situ deposition of Ir NCs at 300 /C14 C on two different Al 2O3 surfaces. The Ir (III) acetylacetonate (Ir(acac)3) precursor was kept at 200 /C14 C with a vapor pressure of 1–2 millibars, 28–30 and the gas mixture (49% O2 þ 51% N2) used as the O 2 precursor was transferred into the reactor with a flow rate of 40 sccm. The Ir(acac) 3 and O2 precursors were pulsed for 1.5 and 0.7 s, respectively, followed by N 2 purges 5 s in duration.
